faq.q: Dener, NovoTech or Senfeng — which laser should I buy?
faq.a: Dener is the premium line: Turkish-built, with Precitec heads, IPG / nLIGHT sources and a heavier frame rated for 1.5 G, parts stocked in Canada and the longer life at high duty — the machine for a job shop that cuts two shifts a day. NovoTech's own value line is built in China to our specification — Raycus or IPG sources, Cypcut controls, Hiwin, YYC and Schneider components — at the lowest price of the three, in open, enclosed exchange-table, ground-rail and sheet-and-tube versions to 60 kW. Senfeng is a value line under its own brand from a very large Chinese manufacturer (about 15,000 machines a year) that builds its own sources and heads, CE / FDA / ETL certified, with the widest range: 4 × 4 ft compact machines, 80 kW, 3D and coil-fed lasers. All three are sold, installed and supported by NovoTech with the same CSA panel and warranty; we quote them side by side so you can compare.

faq.q: What laser power do I need?
faq.a: Power sets the thickness and the speed. As a guide for mild steel: 3 kW cuts 1/2″, 6 kW 3/4″ (and 1/4″ at over 300 in/min), 12 kW 1″, 20 kW 1-1/4″ and 30 – 40 kW 1-1/2″ and beyond; stainless and aluminum run about 20 – 30 % thinner at the same power, with nitrogen or air assist. Most Canadian job shops buying today choose 6 or 12 kW: thick enough for structural work, fast enough to pay for the machine on thin sheet. Tell us your material mix and we run the cutting chart for you.

faq.q: Which table size?
faq.a: The model number is the nominal working area in centimetres: 3015 = 10 × 5 ft (3,000 × 1,500 mm) — a standard 4 × 8 or 5 × 10 sheet; 4020 = 13 × 6.6 ft; 6020 = 20 × 6.6 ft for 6 × 20 plate; 6025 and 8025 = 20 and 26 ft × 8.2 ft; 12526 = 41 × 8.5 ft. The 5 × 10 machine is the Canadian standard; buy the 6020 if you cut 20 ft plate or want to nest several sheets without reloading; the 4 × 4 ft Senfeng compact is for small parts in a small shop.

faq.q: Single table, double table or pallet changer?
faq.a: A single-table machine (Dener Smart open and semi-closed, NovoTech ULF, Senfeng compact and NP) stops while you unload and load — fine for a few sheets an hour and the lowest price. A double table or pallet changer (Dener GFL and Smart closed, NovoTech ULE, Senfeng H series) swaps tables in 15 to 20 seconds, so the laser cuts while the operator loads: the difference between 40 and 70 % spindle time on a busy machine, and the base for a loading tower later.

faq.q: What about assist gas and fume extraction?
faq.a: Oxygen gives the fastest cut and an oxide edge on mild steel; nitrogen a clean, paint-ready edge on all metals; compressed air at 16 bar replaces nitrogen on sheet to about 1/4″ and cuts the gas bill to near zero — the intelligent air-cutting package is an option on both lines. The machines have pneumatic extraction compartments under the table and connect to a dust collector, which we can supply.

faq.q: Can the laser be automated?
faq.a: Yes — a loading / unloading tower that feeds the pallet changer, sheet storage with several shelves for lights-out production, part sorting, and bevel heads for weld preparation. The Dener GFL and closed-type Smart, the NovoTech ULE and the Senfeng H series are prepared for the tower; the Senfeng coil-fed lines go further and cut straight from the coil. Ask us for the automation layout.

faq.q: What does the machine need on site?
faq.a: A level floor, 600 V 3-phase (with the transformer we supply) or 480 V, a chiller (included), assist gas, a dust collector and a compressed-air supply for air cutting. A 6 kW 3015 draws about 30 kW in total and needs roughly 33 × 20 ft with a pallet changer. Delivery, installation and operator training are done by NovoTech from Mississauga, ON, Canada, and the Ontario pre-start health and safety review is prepared by us.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

NovoTech sells three lines of fiber lasers in Canada, each on its own page: the Dener lasers — the premium line, made in Turkey, the GFL production laser with a 1.5 G gantry and pallet changer and the Smart series to 13 × 82 ft, 3 to 40 kW; NovoTech's own value line — the open ULF single-table lasers, the enclosed ULE with a 15-second exchange table, the ULG ground-rail plate lasers, the ULFT and ULET that cut sheet and tube on one machine, and plate tables to 85 ft with up to 60 kW; and the Senfeng lasers — a value line under its own brand, from 4 × 4 ft compact machines and the NP open-type to the H series with pallet changer to 80 kW, plate gantries to 10 × 164 ft, 3D and coil-fed lines. faq.q: Dener, NovoTech or Senfeng — which tube laser should I buy?
faq.a: Dener's E-FTL and FTL are the premium machines — Turkish-built, 1 G servo chucks, Precitec heads, ±0.05 mm, parts stocked in Canada — for the shop that runs the tube laser all day on precise work. NovoTech's own ULT is the value line we build to our specification: two or three pneumatic chucks for the Ø0.4 to 14.2″ tube most shops cut, at the lowest price of the three. Senfeng's tube lasers are a value line under their own brand: a 6 m two-chuck machine with a 1.5 kW source costs a fraction of a premium tube laser and cuts the railings, frames and furniture tube most shops run, and the range goes where few others do — zero-tailing three-chuck machines, four-chuck machines for 49 ft stock, Ø25″ pipe and the H-beam profile line. We quote all three so you can compare.

faq.q: What can a tube laser cut?
faq.a: Round, square, rectangular, oval and open profiles — angle, channel, flat bar — in mild steel, stainless, aluminum, copper and brass, from the chuck's minimum to its maximum size, in wall thicknesses to about 1/2″ (12 kW) or 3/4″ (20 kW). Holes, slots, copes for tube-to-tube joints, tabs and notches for folding, engraving — anything you can draw on the surface of the profile. A 5-axis or 45° bevel head adds weld preparations and mitred corners.

faq.q: Two, three or four chucks?
faq.a: Two chucks (Dener E-FTL / FTL, NovoTech ULT, Senfeng T / PLUS) hold the bar at both ends and cover tube to Ø25″ — the machine most shops need. A third chuck in the middle (NovoTech ULT three-chuck, Senfeng NT) takes over the bar as it shortens, so the last part is cut without a tail. Three and four chucks on the heavy machines (Senfeng ST / HT) carry 49 ft bars of 6,600 lb without sag for structural sections and towers.

faq.q: How is the tube loaded?
faq.a: From a bundle: the automatic loader separates one bar, measures it and feeds it to the rear chuck; the front chuck and following supports hold the bar as it is cut; finished parts drop onto the unloading table or conveyor and the remnant is ejected. One operator runs the machine while loading the next bundle. Loading lengths of 7, 9 and 12 m — or manual loading on the small Senfeng T series.

faq.q: What about software?
faq.a: The CNC imports STEP / IGES solid models of the tube parts, unfolds them onto the profile, nests them along the bar to use the remnant and writes the program — with the cutting database for the material and seam detection to orient welded tube. Offline programming on a PC is standard on both lines.

faq.q: Floor space and power?
faq.a: A 7 m machine needs about 20 m (65 ft) of length including the loader and unloader; a 12 m machine about 30 m. 600 V 3-phase with the supplied transformer or 480 V, a chiller (included), assist gas and a dust collector. We lay the machine out for your building before you order.

Manual machines have no electrics.

faq.q: GFL or Smart — what is the difference?
faq.a: Both come from Dener's Kayseri plant with the same sources, heads and software. The GFL is the production machine: a heavier stress-relieved frame and space-frame bridge rated for 1.5 G, a pallet changer and the full option list — the machine for two shifts a day. The Smart series is built to a lower price: the closed-type still has a double exchange table and 1 G, the semi-closed machines offer very large single tables, and the open-type is the entry-level 3 – 6 kW laser. Same cut quality; the GFL is faster between parts and lasts longer at high duty.

faq.q: Which Smart — closed, semi-closed or open?
faq.a: Closed-type when you cut all day: the double exchange table keeps the laser cutting while you load, and the cabin keeps fumes and the beam inside. Semi-closed when the parts are long — 20 to 82 ft single tables for beams, ship sections and plate that no standard laser takes. Open-type when the budget comes first and the sheets are loaded by hand or forklift from any side: 3 or 6 kW, 5 × 10 to 6.6 × 20 ft, the lowest-priced Dener laser.

faq.q: What is in a Dener laser as standard?
faq.a: An IPG, Raycus or nLIGHT fiber source, a Precitec or Raytools autofocus cutting head with capacitive height sensing and collision protection, a stress-relieved welded frame, pneumatic fume-extraction compartments under the table and scrap boxes on wheels, a chiller, a CNC with nesting software, cutting database and production reports, and a remote handset. Cutting gas regulators, dust collector connections and the CSA-approved panel with a 600 V transformer are included in the NovoTech package.

faq.q: What can be added later?
faq.a: A loading / unloading tower that feeds the pallet changer, sheet storage with several shelves for lights-out production, part sorting, a bevel head for weld preparation, a marking head, and the intelligent air-cutting package that replaces nitrogen on sheet to about 1/4″. The GFL and the closed-type Smart are prepared for the tower from the factory.

Senfeng builds its own sources and heads and sells for less, with a range Dener does not cover (4 × 4 ft compact machines, 60 kW plate gantries, sheet-and-tube combos, coil-fed lines). faq.q: Open ULF or enclosed ULE?
faq.a: The ULF is the open machine: a single table loaded from three sides, the lowest price per kilowatt and the right choice for a shop that cuts a few hours a day and unloads by hand. The ULE puts the cutting area in a full enclosure — laser-safe windows, fumes extracted from inside the cabin, less noise — and adds an exchange table that swaps in 15 seconds, so the laser cuts while the operator loads the next sheet. Above 6 kW, for two shifts, or with a storage tower in mind, buy the ULE.

faq.q: ULF-G or ULF-E?
faq.a: Both are open single-table lasers. The G build takes 1.5 to 6 kW and moves at 295 ft/min with 1.4 G — plenty for sheet and light plate. The E build has a heavier frame for 1.5 to 12 kW, 459 ft/min and 1.7 G, a 7.2 ft wide table option (4022E, 6022E) and higher table loads; the large-format E machines from 20 × 8.5 to 85 × 10.5 ft take 6 to 60 kW for plate. Choose the E if you plan to go above 6 kW later or cut thick plate every day.

faq.q: What thickness does each laser power cut?
faq.a: As a guide for mild steel cut with oxygen: 3 kW cuts to 3/4″ (20 mm), 6 kW to 1″ (25 mm), 12 kW to 1-3/16″ (30 mm), and 20 to 30 kW to 2 – 2-3/8″ (50 – 60 mm). The production thickness — where the edge is clean and the speed pays — is about two-thirds of the maximum, and stainless and aluminum cut with nitrogen run thinner at the same power. Most Canadian job shops buying today choose 6 or 12 kW; we send the cutting-speed chart for your material with the quote.

faq.q: When does a ground-rail laser make sense?
faq.a: When the plate is longer than about 40 ft, wider than 10 ft or heavier than a table machine carries. On the ULG the gantry runs on rails set in the floor and the plate lies on a separate support table, so the table takes up to 202,000 lb (91.8 t) — a 2″ plate the full 85 × 14.8 ft weighs about 103,000 lb — without loading the axes. Structural, bridge, tower, mining and heavy-equipment fabricators use it for thick plate that used to go to plasma or oxy-fuel. It needs a prepared foundation for the rails, crane access along the table and extraction sized to the cutting zones; we plan the layout with you. The ULG-A is the faster gantry (262 ft/min, 1.1 G); the ULG-C leaves 11.8″ under the beam with a 60 kW source.

faq.q: Sheet and tube on one machine — ULFT or ULET?
faq.a: Both add a pneumatic rotary chuck and tube supports to the sheet laser: round, square and rectangular tube to Ø8.7″ or Ø13.8″ and 20, 29.5 or 39 ft long, cut with the same source and head. The ULFT is the open version on the ULF table, to 85 × 10.5 ft and 60 kW; the ULET is the enclosed version with the exchange table, to 41 × 8.5 ft and 40 kW. A shop that cuts tube every day is better served by a dedicated ULT tube laser with a loader.

faq.q: What does the laser need on site?
faq.a: Three-phase power (600 V with the CSA panel, or 208 / 240 / 480 V on request), compressed air at 185 psi (13 bar) and 53 cfm (1.5 m³/min) for air cutting, oxygen and nitrogen of 99.96 % purity, a dust collector, and a shop between 41 and 86 °F (5 – 30 °C) with humidity under 70 % — the water chiller is included. We lay the machine out for your building and size the compressor and dust collector with the quote.

Senfeng is a value line sold under its own brand, with the widest range — 4 × 4 ft compact machines, 80 kW, 3D and coil-fed lasers. The NovoTech lasers are our own brand, built in China to our specification with Raycus or IPG sources, Cypcut controls and Hiwin, YYC and Schneider components, at the lowest price of the three; all are installed, warranted and serviced by the same NovoTech technicians. We quote all three so you can compare.

faq.q: Which Senfeng laser for a first machine?
faq.a: For most shops the SF1530 series or the SF3015NP: a 5 × 10 ft single table with 3 or 6 kW. The SF1530NP is fully enclosed with a lifting door and a pull-out table — the tidy choice for a shop that cuts a few hours a day; the SF3015NP is the open-type with loading from three sides and the lowest price per kilowatt. Choose 6 kW if you cut 1/4″ to 1/2″ regularly; 3 kW is enough for sheet to 3/16″. Step up to the H series when you need the pallet changer to keep the laser cutting while you load.

faq.q: NP or H series?
faq.a: The NP is a single-table open machine: the operator loads between sheets, which is fine for a few sheets an hour. The H series is enclosed and has a pallet changer that swaps tables in 20 seconds, so loading overlaps cutting — a production machine for two shifts, with 1.5 to 80 kW and tables to 8.3 × 40 ft, and the one that takes the loading tower and sheet storage. HC is the compact build, H4 the fourth-generation machine with 2 G and 656 ft/min, H5 the heavy-load frame for 40 – 80 kW and 2″ plate.

faq.q: Own-brand sources and heads — what does that mean for support?
faq.a: Senfeng builds its own fiber sources, cutting heads and control cabinets, so parts come from one maker rather than three, and IPG, Raycus or Max sources can be specified instead. Senfeng Laser USA holds parts and has a service team; NovoTech installs, trains and services in Canada from Mississauga, ON, Canada, with remote diagnostics through the control and a CSA-approved panel on every machine.

faq.q: What is the HM sheet-and-tube combination?
faq.a: An enclosed H series sheet laser with a rotary chuck and tube supports on the side: the same 6 to 30 kW source and head cut 5 × 10 to 8.3 × 20 ft sheet with the pallet changer and round, square or rectangular tube from Ø0.7 to 8.6″ and 20 ft long. For a shop that cuts both but cannot justify two machines — switching takes the time to load the tube.

faq.q: Plate gantries, bevels and oxy-fuel?
faq.a: The R and TX series are gantry lasers with 10 and 13 ft wide tables from 20 to 164 ft long and 6 to 60 kW sources, replacing plasma and flame cutting of plate to 2″ and beyond. The TX carries a ±45° bevel head so weld preparations are cut in the same pass; the TXP adds an oxy-fuel torch for plate to 4″ on the same table. Shipyards, structural steel, bridges and heavy equipment are the customers.

faq.q: When does a coil-fed line pay off?
faq.a: When the same thin material runs all day: enclosures, HVAC, appliance and automotive parts. The decoiler, leveller and laser work on one control, there is no sheet handling, no offcuts and no limit on part length. The SF15015C runs thin coil through an open-type laser; the SF1503CH takes coil to 1/8″ and 16.5 tons; the SF2012CH levels and cuts 5/16″ to 9/16″ plate from 22-ton coils with 12 to 80 kW.

faq.q: How does Senfeng compare with the Dener premium line?
faq.a: Dener is the premium line: Turkish-built with Precitec heads, IPG / nLIGHT sources, a heavier frame rated for 1.5 G and parts stocked in Canada — the longer life at high duty. Senfeng costs less and covers sizes and powers Dener does not: 4 × 4 ft compact machines, 60 kW plate gantries, sheet-and-tube combos, 3D and coil-fed lasers. The comparison, the laser power guide and the capacity table for both lines are on the sheet laser cutters overview.

Manual machines have no electrics.

Loading towers, sheet storage and air-cutting packages for every model. Installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada, with a CSA-approved panel and NovoTech's warranty.

faq.q: E-FTL or FTL?
faq.a: The E-FTL is the fast machine for the sizes most fabricators use — railings, frames, furniture, trailers, exhaust — Ø0.3″ to 13.8″, accelerating at 1 G and running 394 ft/min on the small chucks. The FTL is built for weight: structural tube and pipe to Ø25.2″ and 12 m bars of 2,600 kg, with ±0.1 mm repeatability on the large chucks. Both take the same 3 – 20 kW sources and bundle loaders.

faq.q: Which chuck size?
faq.a: The number is the largest round tube in millimetres: E-FTL 120 takes Ø0.3 – 4.7″, 180 to 7.1″, 250 to 9.8″ and 350 to 13.8″; FTL 250, 350, 500 and 640 take Ø0.6″ to 9.8, 13.8, 19.7 and 25.2″. Square and rectangular tube is limited by the diagonal, so a 350 chuck takes about 9.8″ square. Buy the chuck for the largest tube you cut regularly — a smaller chuck is faster and holds thin tube better — and the bar length (7, 9 or 12 m) for the stock you buy.

faq.q: Can it cut bevels and weld preparations?
faq.a: Yes — the 5-axis head on the FTL (optional on the E-FTL) tilts to ±45° so mitred corners, chamfers and weld preparations are cut in the same pass as the holes and copes; the tube arrives at the welding table ready to fit. The seam detector orients welded tube so the seam sits where the drawing puts it.

faq.q: How does Dener compare with the Senfeng value line?
faq.a: Dener's E-FTL and FTL are the premium machines — Turkish-built, 1 G servo chucks, Precitec heads, parts stocked in Canada. Senfeng's tube lasers are the value line: a 6 m two-chuck machine with a 1.5 kW source costs a fraction of a premium tube laser, and the range goes to zero-tailing three-chuck and four-chuck machines for 49 ft stock. The comparison and the capacity table for both lines are on the tube laser cutters overview.

faq.q: Floor space and power?
faq.a: A 7 m E-FTL needs about 20 m (65 ft) of length including the loader and unloader; a 12 m FTL about 30 m. 600 V 3-phase with the supplied transformer or 480 V, a chiller (included), assist gas and a dust collector. We lay the machine out for your building before you order.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

dener-tube-lasers.intro: Dener's tube lasers are the premium line of NovoTech's tube laser section: built in Kayseri, Turkey, with servo chucks, Precitec heads and 3 to 20 kW sources, and backed by parts stocked in Canada. The E-FTL is the fast machine for the sizes most fabricators use — railings, frames, furniture, trailers, exhaust: four chuck sizes from Ø0.3″ to 13.8″, servo axes accelerating at 1 G to 394 ft/min and ±0.05 mm repeatability on 7, 9 or 12 m bars. The FTL is built for weight: structural tube, pipe and beams to Ø25.2″ and 12 m bars of 2,600 kg — 12,000 kg on the long-bed 250 — with ±0.1 mm on the large chucks and a 5-axis bevel head for weld preparations. faq.q: Which ULT chuck size do I need?
faq.a: Size the chuck to the largest tube you cut. The 016 takes round tube from Ø0.4 to 6.3″ and square to 6.3″ — furniture, fitness equipment, racking and railings; the 024 takes Ø9.4″ and square to 8.9″, the size most fabrication shops buy; the 028 takes Ø11″ and the 036 Ø14.2″ and square to 13.8″, with bars to 2,205 lb for structural tube and pipe. The smaller chucks turn faster — 53.5 rpm against 23 rpm on the 036 — and accelerate harder, so they are quicker on small tube.

faq.q: Two chucks or three?
faq.a: With two chucks the rear chuck has to keep hold of the bar, so the last few inches of every bar are scrap. The three-chuck ULT adds a chuck that takes over the bar as it shortens and cuts the last part with no remnant — on 20 to 39 ft bars of stainless or heavy-wall tube that saves material on every bundle. It is built on the 024, 028 and 036 chucks.

faq.q: How is the tube loaded?
faq.a: The pneumatic loader of the 016 and 024 machines separates one bar from the rack and feeds it to the rear chuck — round tube to Ø8.7″ and square to 8.7″ across the corners. The automatic feeding system takes bundles of up to 5 tonnes and bars up to 606 lb (275 kg), sorting and positioning each bar in a 19-second cycle. The heavy tube of the 028 and 036 machines is placed on the infeed supports by crane. Finished parts slide onto the unloading table.

faq.q: Can it cut bevels for welding?
faq.a: Yes — the optional five-axis head tilts ±45°, so weld preparations, mitred corners and tube-to-tube copes are cut in the same pass as the holes and the parting cut. The standard head cuts square to the tube wall.

faq.q: What about software?
faq.a: The Cypcut tube control holds the cutting database and adjusts the power to the speed through corners. TubesT, BOCHU's tube nesting software, imports the 3D parts, unfolds them onto the profile and nests them along the bar to use the remnant; it is an option and also runs on a PC in the office.

faq.q: How does the ULT compare with the Dener and Senfeng tube lasers?
faq.a: Dener's E-FTL and FTL are the premium machines — built in Turkey with 1 G servo chucks and parts stocked in Canada — and the FTL goes to Ø25.2″. Senfeng's value line covers Ø0.5 to 25″ with three- and four-chuck machines and an H-beam line. The ULT is NovoTech's own tube laser for the sizes most shops cut, Ø0.4 to 14.2″, at the lowest price of the three; every model of the three lines is in one table on the tube laser cutters overview.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

faq.q: T series or PLUS?
faq.a: The T series is the all-round two-chuck machine: 1.5 to 6 kW, Ø0.5 to 14″, 20 to 39 ft, fifteen models — the one most shops buy first. The PLUS is tuned for speed on small and medium tube — 394 to 492 ft/min, 180 rpm chucks, 3 to 6 kW — for furniture, fitness equipment and racking where thousands of short parts are cut a shift. If you also need mitres and weld preparations, the GPLUS (Ø0.6 – 4.7″) or GT (Ø2.3 – 14.1″) add the 45° bevel head.

faq.q: What is zero-tailing — the NT series?
faq.a: A two-chuck machine cannot cut the last part of the bar because the rear chuck has to hold something, so a remnant of the chuck length is scrapped from every bar. The NT puts a third chuck in the middle that takes over the bar as it shortens, so the last part is cut and the tail is near zero — on 20 to 39 ft stock to Ø14″ that is several percent of material saved on every bundle.

faq.q: When do I need three or four chucks — ST and HT?
faq.a: When the tube is long and heavy: the ST (three chucks) and HT (four chucks) carry tube to Ø25″ and 6,600 lb over 29 to 49 ft without sag, so round, square and large rectangular sections for structural steel, towers, cranes and trailers are cut straight and square. Sources of 6 to 20 kW cut walls to 3/4″; bevel heads and automatic loaders are available. The SF1500CH is the version for H-beams, channels and angles, with a camera that scans each beam before cutting.

faq.q: How is the tube loaded and unloaded?
faq.a: From a bundle: the automatic loader separates one bar, measures it and feeds it to the rear chuck; the front chuck and the following supports hold the bar as it is cut; finished parts drop onto the unloading table or conveyor and the remnant is ejected. The loader is optional on the small T series — many shops start with manual loading — and standard on the heavy machines.

faq.q: What about software?
faq.a: The bus-based CNC imports STEP / IGES solid models or draws the parts in its own tube CAD, unfolds them onto the profile, nests them along the bar to use the remnant and writes the program, with a cutting database for the material and seam detection to orient welded tube. Offline programming on a PC is standard.

faq.q: How does Senfeng compare with the Dener premium line?
faq.a: Dener's E-FTL and FTL are the premium machines — Turkish-built, 1 G servo chucks, Precitec heads, parts stocked in Canada. Senfeng costs a fraction of that for the same tube sizes and reaches further: zero-tailing three-chuck machines, four-chuck machines for 49 ft stock, Ø25″ pipe and the H-beam line. The comparison and the capacity table for both lines are on the tube laser cutters overview.

Manual machines have no electrics.

The T series two-chuck machines cover Ø0.5 to 14″ and 20 to 39 ft with 1.5 to 6 kW; the PLUS runs to 492 ft/min on small tube and the GPLUS / GT add a 45° bevel head for mitred corners and weld preparations; the NT puts a third chuck in the middle so the last part is cut without a tail; and the ST three-chuck and HT four-chuck machines carry tube to Ø25″ and 6,600 lb over 29 to 49 ft with 6 to 20 kW, for structural steel, towers, cranes and trailers. The SF1500CH is the profile line for H-beams, channels and angles.
